findings.description: SHEET-MARK-005's second clause ('while offline, the kernels shall use the last cached marks with their quote-epoch stamps') is NOT implemented inside sheets-view. The real `read_marks` only propagates the transport `Err` when `read_price_pass` fails (test: `transport_failure_propagates_error_does_not_emit_empty_marks` asserts `result.is_err()` and nothing more). The function's own doc comment says the actual cached-mark substitution is 'runtime's: on Err, runtime retains its existing cached marks... and re-injects them into the next replay' — i.e. delegated to a crate not present in this audit, and untested here. All three A-outputs, forced to interpret the spec sentence without visibility into this crate boundary, invented and implemented the offline-fallback logic locally as though it belonged in this module: A1's `MarkCache::get_for_offline_kernel`, A2's `resolve_mark(... online: bool ...)` branch that returns the cached mark when `!online`, A3's `MarkCache::resolve` returning `self.last_good.get(&symbol_id)` when no fresh non-degraded mark exists. All three B-outputs, reading only the real code, correctly reconstructed the propagate-don't-substitute behavior, and B3 explicitly flagged 'Offline mark carry-forward is the caller's (runtime's) responsibility, out of this function's scope.' Same gap surfaced from both directions: the spec states a behavior this crate's code does not perform (or verify) itself.

The code's actual 'use a cached mark with its original stamp' mechanism is triggered by a PER-SYMBOL bounded-poll timeout (a price cell staying `Transient` through `SettleConfig.max_polls`), not by system-wide 'offline' as SHEET-MARK-005 frames it — and when this fires, the symbol is explicitly NOT recorded degraded (test `transient_keeps_prior_mark_and_retries_degrades_only_after_window` asserts `produced.degraded.get("AMZN").is_none()`), so the stale carried-forward price flows into `to_ledger_marks()` looking like an ordinary fresh mark and never reaches ledger-core's per-symbol degradation (LEDGER-PNL-007) at all — contradicting a literal reading of clause 1 ('a degraded symbol mark shall feed... degradation') for this case. All three A-outputs, reading the spec's single merged sentence, treat 'degraded' and 'stale/carried-forward' as the same thing that always feeds degradation (e.g. A3's degradation is cleared only by 'a subsequent healthy mark,' implying anything else, including a carried-forward stale mark, stays flagged). All three B-outputs independently reconstructed from the code that these are two distinct, oppositely-reported branches (TimedOut-with-no-prior → degraded; TimedOut-with-prior → silently NOT degraded), a distinction none of the A-outputs anticipated.

The spec phrase 'quote-epoch stamps' pushed all three A-outputs to invent an opaque monotonic tick-counter type (A1/A3's `QuoteEpoch = u64` 'bumped per read-back cycle', A2's `QuoteEpoch(pub u64)`), each explicitly reasoning that GOOGLEFINANCE has no reliable per-cell fetch time so a counter was chosen over a timestamp. The real code's stamp is a calendar `Date` (`Mark.quote_date`), produced by an elaborate `quote_date_formula` that truncates GOOGLEFINANCE's `tradetime` to a locale-proof day-serial specifically so it is 'never wall-clock read time' — a real calendar date, not a generation/tick counter. All three B-outputs converged on reconstructing this as an explicit rule ('a settled Mark's quote_date shall be the GOOGLEFINANCE-supplied quote date... never wall-clock read time'). The spec's own vocabulary ('epoch') is misaligned with the type and mechanism the code actually uses, and both directions latched onto different, non-matching interpretations of it.

notes: Read the real files directly (lib.rs, testkit.rs, tests/marks.rs) rather than relying solely on the six sketches. Two lower-confidence assumption artifacts I deliberately did NOT promote to findings: (1) all three A-outputs model the 'feed degradation' clause as an explicit push/callback (DegradationSink trait or equivalent), whereas the real mechanism is passive omission from `to_ledger_marks()`'s BTreeMap — but SHEET-MARK-005's text never specifies push vs. pull, so this divergence has no textual anchor and is an assumption artifact, not a finding. (2) A1/A3 model degradation as sticky per-symbol state requiring an explicit clear; the real `MarksProduced` is recomputed fresh every `read_marks` call with no persisted degradation state in this crate — again unanimous but not clearly forced by spec text (LEDGER-PNL-007's own persistence, which would matter here, lives in ledger-core and isn't visible to either direction). Both were considered but left out as filtered assumption noise per the classification instructions. The three B-outputs also reconstructed several rules clearly unrelated to SHEET-MARK-005 specifically (the round-half-to-even cent-conversion formula/scale, SubCent vs Permanent classification of price_to_cents, the Permanent-settles-immediately vs TimedOut-after-window distinction, max_polls=8) — these are real, well-agreed B-side pins but they answer sibling SHEET-MARK-* requirements, not the one given for comparison, so I excluded them from the findings list even though they'd count as strong B-ONLY-DRIFT against a broader spec selection.
